title: Isandro and the Cipher
premise: When the coffin of Aldous Vey, founder of the fog-bound town of Marrow Bay, is exhumed for a memorial reburial and found empty, concierge Ulyana Nystrom is drawn in because the exhumation order was mailed from her own hotel. Following a thirty-year-old cipher hidden in Vey's published letters, she discovers that Vey faked his death to escape prosecution, that several of the town's founding families helped bury the secret, and that one of them is now killing to keep it buried. Ulyana deciphers the final letter to locate the living Vey — now a dying caretaker at her own hotel under another name — and must choose between handing him to justice and protecting the chosen family of hotel staff who sheltered him. In the end she exposes the true murderer, lets Vey die as the man he became rather than the criminal he was, and closes the case on her own terms.
about_author: Oscar Nystrom is a former night auditor who spent a decade working the front desks of coastal hotels, collecting the small betrayals and quiet kindnesses of strangers. Isandro and the Cipher is their second mystery featuring concierge Ulyana Nystrom.

chapters.title: The Guest Who Never Slept
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. A routine shift at the Saltglass Hotel: Ulyana notices a gaunt longtime guest, 'Mr. Ilya,' who signs his register with an odd looping mark. Establishes her gift for observation and her loyalty to her ragtag staff family. Emotional beat: pride and control before the world cracks.

chapters.title: An Empty Suit of Local Hero
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. The town gathers for the ceremonial exhumation of founder Aldous Vey; the coffin holds only stones and a rotted coat. The crowd's grief curdles into suspicion. Ulyana recognizes the exhumation paperwork's return address: her own hotel, room 214. Emotional beat: vertigo — her sanctuary implicated.

chapters.title: Room 214
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. She searches 214 and finds nothing but a pressed violet and a page torn from Vey's published memoirs, one letter circled. Sheriff Dane Corliss arrives and pointedly asks where she was last Tuesday. Emotional beat: first taste of being a suspect.

chapters.title: The Cipher in the Letters
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: Ulyana and archivist Petra Osei. Petra reveals Vey's memoirs contain recurring misprinted letters across editions — a cipher only visible by comparing printings. Someone has been quietly buying up old copies for years. Emotional beat: intellectual thrill, the case truly opens.

chapters.title: Thirty Years of Alibis
chapters.summary: Ulyana interviews the four surviving founding families — the Hales, the Merricks, the Corlisses, and the Vane sisters. Each has an airtight alibi for the week Vey supposedly died, each too perfect. Emotional beat: unease; perfection itself becomes evidence.

chapters.title: What the Night Staff Saw
chapters.summary: Night porter Samir's POV. Samir admits he let a stranger into the archive room weeks ago — a woman with a Vane family ring. He begs Ulyana not to fire him; she instead pulls him onto the case. Emotional beat: found family deepens; trust as strategy.

chapters.title: The First Copy Burns
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. The historical society's set of Vey's memoirs goes up in flames hours after Petra catalogs them. Arson, but no body. Ulyana realizes someone is erasing the cipher edition by edition. Emotional beat: the clock starts ticking.

chapters.title: A Grave Without a Body, a Body Without a Grave
chapters.summary: Sheriff Corliss POV. A fresh corpse surfaces in the marsh: Hale patriarch Edmund Hale, dead three days, clutching a scrap of violet-scented paper. Corliss, son of one of the alibi families, suppresses details. Emotional beat: rot beneath respectability.

chapters.title: The Mark on the Register
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. She matches Mr. Ilya's looping signature to the circled letters in the memoirs — the signature IS part of the cipher key. Her quiet guest is either the killer or the reason for the killings. Emotional beat: dread and fascination entwined.

chapters.title: Petra's Missing Year
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Flashback chapter: Petra arrived in Marrow Bay thirty years ago as a child the Vane sisters quietly took in — meaning the archivist has skin in the founding families' secrets. She confesses a fragment to Ulyana. Emotional beat: loyalty tested by buried history.

chapters.title: The Vane Sisters' Parlor
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. The elderly Vane sisters serve tea and lies; one lets slip that Vey didn't die in '92 — he 'went to sea.' Their brother Rowan Vane, town coroner, watches Ulyana leave. Emotional beat: the mask of gentility slipping.

chapters.title: Second Fire, First Warning
chapters.summary: Samir's POV. The hotel's back office burns overnight; inside, someone leaves a note in cipher: STOP READING HIM. Ulyana decodes it using the signature key and realizes the killer knows she's close — and knows the hotel. Emotional beat: fear invades the sanctuary.

chapters.title: Corliss Closes Ranks
chapters.summary: Corliss POV. The sheriff names Ulyana a person of interest, freezing her out of official channels. He privately burns his father's old letters. Emotional beat: a man drowning in inherited guilt, half villain, half victim.

chapters.title: The Undercroft
chapters.summary: Ulyana and Petra's POV. Deciphered letters point to an undercroft beneath the old cannery: ledgers proving Vey embezzled the town's founding trust and framed an immigrant dockworker for it — the injustice the families covered up. Emotional beat: righteous anger; the theme of justice outside the law crystallizes.

chapters.title: Rowan Makes His Offer
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Coroner Rowan Vane corners her: help him find Vey's hiding place and split whatever the old man left, or join Hale in the marsh. He reveals the killer isn't him — he's being blackmailed too. Emotional beat: menace and moral fog.

chapters.title: Ilya's Last Night
chapters.summary: Mr. Ilya's POV. The dying guest reveals himself: he is Aldous Vey, hiding thirty years in plain sight, cared for by the hotel staff who never asked questions. He gives Ulyana the final letter but refuses to run. Emotional beat: pity, fury, and strange tenderness.

chapters.title: The Letter That Names Him
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. The final cipher letter doesn't hide Vey — it names his blackmailer: the person who discovered the empty coffin scheme decades ago and has fed on the secret since. All clues point somewhere Ulyana refuses to look: her own staff. Emotional beat: betrayal's cold draft.

chapters.title: The One Who Noticed Everything
chapters.summary: Samir's POV. The blackmailer is revealed: head housekeeper Marta, who as a child lost her father — the framed dockworker — and has spent thirty years extorting the founding families while hunting Vey. She killed Hale when he tried to confess publicly. Emotional beat: heartbreak; the villain is family.

chapters.title: Standoff at the Cannery
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Marta lures Vey to the cannery to kill him before he can testify; Ulyana trades herself as hostage, stalling until Petra and Samir arrive with the sheriff — whom Ulyana has secretly fed the suppressed evidence. Climax: violence, confession, Marta's collapse. Emotional beat: everything on the line.

chapters.title: Justice, Informally
chapters.summary: Ulyana and Corliss POV. Marta is arrested; the founding families' cover-up goes public, gutting Marrow Bay's mythology. Corliss resigns rather than bury his father's complicity. Ulyana declines credit, keeping the hotel out of the record. Emotional beat: bitter, earned catharsis.

chapters.title: The Second Funeral
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Vey dies peacefully days later; the staff bury him under his assumed name in the hotel garden, no law informed. Ulyana writes the death certificate herself, in cipher. Emotional beat: mourning on their own terms; identity chosen, not given.

chapters.title: Concierge, Closing Time
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV, epilogue. A new guest checks in carrying a copy of Vey's memoirs with fresh marginalia. Ulyana smiles, slides the register across the desk, and says welcome to the Saltglass. Emotional beat: quiet resolve — the next case is already knocking, and she will close it too.
